geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the existing hall around a genuine courtyard/public void so the neighborhood program gains a usable social center and clearer ground threshold.
Open the void toward the verified access side to establish an active frontage response.
Create a bounded but substantial court rather than a decorative notch.

graph_edits.rationale: Introduce a real public void/court in the protected section controller so the ground threshold can become legible and usable rather than a hidden puncture.
Align the court opening to the program-frame side corresponding to the verified access edge so the frontage can read as public.
Keep the void bounded and inhabitable rather than collapsing the mass into a thin sculptural shell.

rationale: The candidate is visible as one dominant mass, but the four views reveal a narrow, twisted, ramp-like wedge that is coherent mainly as a sculptural profile rather than as a plausible neighborhood-living building. The verified access edge is met with a mostly sealed or oblique response; there is no strong public threshold, court, notch, or ground seam aligned to that frontage. The void logic is weak: the BOOK puncture reads as internal subtraction rather than a legible usable open-space figure. The form also behaves more like a stacked/tapered hall or tower fragment than a compact active-edge mixed-use bar, so the program contract is not satisfied. The silhouette is continuous, but the section reads arbitrary and stair-like rather than capacity-bearing or terrace-based. Overall this fails program_fit_hard_pass despite decent single-gesture clarity.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Stepped/tapered mixed-use massing can read as a strong singular gesture when the section is coherent.
